name: nextrmnl
description: nextrmnl is SSH and SFTP in the browser for the machines in your own network: a terminal (xterm.js) with tabs, jump hosts and copy and paste the way PuTTY does it, plus file transfer next to it. Accounts with a vault each for keys and passwords, sealed with the account's password so that not even the operator can read it. Host keys are checked and remembered, unknown hosts are shown with their fingerprint first. Connections can be shared between accounts without sharing access, sign-in works with a password, an optional second factor from an authenticator app, or OpenID Connect (one-button setup for authentik). By default nextrmnl only connects into private networks. Backups as encrypted ZIP files, a log that never contains terminal content or credentials. The interface is available in English and German.

paths.name: Data (Container Path: /data)
paths.description: Holds the SQLite database with accounts, connections and the sealed vaults, the key secret.key, backups and logs. Keep it on a local disk, not on a network share.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: Port you reach nextrmnl at. Container port: 8000

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User id that should own the files in /data. 99 is the Unraid default.

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group id that should own the files in /data. 100 is the Unraid default.

variables.name: Time Zone
variables.description: Time zone for timestamps in the log and the session history, for example Europe/Berlin. Leave blank for UTC.

variables.name: Public URL
variables.description: The address people use to reach nextrmnl, for example https://nextrmnl.example.com when it sits behind a reverse proxy. Used for invitation links and the return address of OpenID Connect. Leave blank to take the address of the request; the same can be set later under Settings, Sign-in.

variables.name: Container Port (host networking only)
variables.description: Leave this empty unless you switched Network Type to Host. In bridge mode the WebUI Port above already does the job and setting this will break it, because the mapping still points at 8000. On host networking the port inside the container is the port on your server, so use this to move nextrmnl off 8000 if something else is already there.

variables.name: Secret Key
variables.description: Protects the server-side secrets (the OpenID Connect client secret, second-factor seeds). Leave blank: nextrmnl creates one on first start and keeps it in /data/secret.key. The vaults do not depend on it; they open with the account's password only.

variables.name: Secure Cookie
variables.description: auto marks the session cookie Secure when the request arrived over https, also behind a proxy that sends X-Forwarded-Proto. Use on only if a proxy terminates TLS and forwards plain http without that header, and never if nextrmnl should also be reachable over http, or nobody can sign in. off never marks it.
